OSI model.defn: Seven layers organising network communication, from physical to application

TCP/IP stack.defn: Four-layer model: application, transport, internet, network access

Encapsulation.defn: Each layer adds its header as data travels down the stack

PDU.defn: Protocol data unit — segment (layer 4), packet (layer 3), frame (layer 2)

Port.defn: Transport-layer address, e.g. 443 for HTTPS, 53 for DNS

MAC address.defn: Physical address burned into the interface, used at layer 2

Subnet mask.defn: Marks the network/host boundary in an IPv4 address

CIDR.defn: Classless notation — the /n count of network bits

VLSM.defn: Variable subnet masks within one major network, largest first

Network address.defn: First address of a range — identifies the subnet, never assigned

Broadcast address.defn: Last address of a range — reaches all hosts, never assigned

Link-local.defn: IPv6 address valid on its subnet only, fe80::/10

Dual-stack.defn: Running IPv4 and IPv6 together — doubles the attack surface

Frame.defn: Layer 2 PDU — Ethernet headers plus payload

Forwarding table.defn: Switch's learned map of MAC addresses to ports

Unknown unicast flooding.defn: Frame sent to all ports but the source when the destination is unknown

VLAN.defn: Logical broadcast domain carved out of a physical switch

Trunk port.defn: Carries many tagged VLANs between switches

Access port.defn: Carries one untagged VLAN to an endpoint

Native VLAN.defn: Untagged VLAN on a trunk — VLAN 1 by default, a known risk

VLAN hopping.defn: Attack crossing VLAN boundaries: switch spoofing or double tagging

Switch spoofing.defn: Attacker negotiates a trunk port to reach many VLANs

Double tagging.defn: Native VLAN spoof that carries a frame into another VLAN

CAM table.defn: Switch's forwarding table; overflow (MAC flooding) degrades it to hub mode

Microsegmentation.defn: Granular segmentation isolating individual workloads, often via SDN

STP.defn: IEEE 802.1D — blocks redundant ports to prevent loops

Root bridge.defn: Switch with the lowest bridge ID (priority + MAC)

BPDU Guard.defn: Shuts down a port that receives BPDUs on an access port

Root Guard.defn: Prevents a port from becoming a root port

DMZ.defn: Segment hosting public-facing services, isolated from internal

Blast radius.defn: The extent of damage a compromise can reach — limited by segmentation

DNS.defn: Translates names to addresses — the internet's directory

A / AAAA record.defn: Name to IPv4 / name to IPv6

MX record.defn: Mail exchange server for a domain

Cache poisoning.defn: Forged DNS response inserted into a resolver's cache

DNS amplification.defn: Small queries drawing large responses — DDoS fuel

DHCP DORA.defn: Discover, Offer, Request, Ack — the address assignment process

DHCP starvation.defn: Spoofed MACs exhausting the address pool

DHCP snooping.defn: Switch filter trusting only authorised DHCP ports

NTP.defn: Network Time Protocol — clock synchronisation, UDP 123

Stratum.defn: Distance from the authoritative time source

SSH.defn: Encrypted remote access replacing Telnet — TCP 22

Key-based auth.defn: Public key stored on the server; private key proves possession

Attack surface.defn: The sum of entry points an attacker can use to enter or extract data

Threat vector.defn: The path or method an attacker uses to reach the attack surface

Confidentiality.defn: Information should only be read by authorised persons

Integrity.defn: Data is stored and transferred as intended; modification requires authorisation

Availability.defn: Information is accessible to those authorised to view or modify it

Non-repudiation.defn: Persons cannot deny creating or modifying data — proof of origin and action

Gap analysis.defn: Comparing current security posture against a target framework to find gaps

Operational control.defn: Depends on a person to implement — training, guards

Technical control.defn: Implemented in systems and software — firewalls, encryption

Physical control.defn: Mediates access to premises and hardware — locks, cameras

Preventive / detective / corrective.defn: Operates before / during / after an attack

Defence in depth.defn: Layered controls so no single point of failure

Least privilege.defn: Users receive only the access they need

Zero trust.defn: Verify every request — never trust implicitly

Vulnerability.defn: A weakness in a system, process or design

Threat.defn: A person, tool or method that could exploit a vulnerability

Risk.defn: The likelihood and impact of a threat exploiting a vulnerability

Threat actor.defn: A person or group that poses a threat

APT.defn: Advanced persistent threat, long-term and strategic, state-backed or highly resourced

Script kiddie.defn: Unskilled attacker using pre-written tools on easy targets

Hacktivist.defn: Hacker promoting a political or social cause

Spear phishing.defn: Targeted, personalised phishing aimed at a named individual

Zero day.defn: A vulnerability unknown to the vendor with no available patch

False flag.defn: Techniques that mislead attribution to another entity

Symmetric encryption.defn: One shared secret key encrypts and decrypts — fast, for bulk data

AES.defn: Advanced Encryption Standard — symmetric; key sizes of 128, 192 or 256 bits

Asymmetric encryption.defn: Public/private key pair — public encrypts, private decrypts

RSA / ECC.defn: Asymmetric algorithms — RSA on factoring; ECC with smaller keys for constrained devices

Keyspace.defn: The range of possible key values; longer keys mean larger keyspaces

Hashing.defn: One-way, fixed-length digest — integrity and password storage; avalanche effect

Digital signature.defn: Hashing plus the private key — integrity, authentication, non-repudiation

PKI.defn: Infrastructure that proves the identity of a public key holder

Registration authority (RA).defn: Verifies identities before the CA issues

CN / SAN.defn: Common Name (legacy FQDN) / Subject Alternative Name (modern, wildcards)

CRL / OCSP.defn: Revocation list / real-time online certificate status protocol

TPM / HSM.defn: Motherboard cryptoprocessor / dedicated hardware security module

Perfect forward secrecy.defn: Ephemeral session keys — compromise cannot decrypt past traffic

Salting / key stretching.defn: Random per-password value / extra hashing rounds against brute force

Steganography / tokenisation.defn: Concealing in a cover file / substituting data with reversible tokens

Ownership factor.defn: Something you have — token, smart card, phone

Biometric factor.defn: Something you are/do — fingerprint, face, voice

MFA.defn: Multifactor authentication — factors from different categories

FRR / FAR.defn: False Rejection Rate (Type I) / False Acceptance Rate (Type II)

Passwordless.defn: Authenticator-held private key plus presence gesture

RBAC.defn: Role-based access control — permissions via roles

SSO.defn: Single sign-on — one authentication, many applications

IdP / SP.defn: Identity provider / service provider in federation

Directory service.defn: Central identity store — Active Directory, LDAP

Provisioning.defn: Creating, modifying and removing accounts through the user lifecycle

PAM.defn: Privileged access management — protects admin accounts

JIT access.defn: Just-in-time access — elevated rights granted only when needed

Identity governance.defn: Access reviews, policy enforcement and audit

SAML / OAuth / OIDC.defn: Assertion protocol / authorisation framework / identity layer

Spine-leaf.defn: Data-centre fabric — every leaf connects to every spine

Least connectivity.defn: Limit connections to what is necessary

Stateless firewall.defn: Checks each packet alone — no connection context

Stateful firewall.defn: State table tracks connections; allows established flows

NGFW.defn: Next-generation firewall — application-aware, with deep packet inspection

IDS / IPS.defn: Detect and alert / detect and block inline

Signature detection.defn: Matches known attack patterns — misses the unknown

Anomaly detection.defn: Flags deviations from a baseline — finds unknowns, more false positives

WAF.defn: Web application firewall — protects web apps at layer 7

NAC.defn: Network access control — endpoint posture before join

Bastion host.defn: Internet-exposed, hardened host for secure administrative access

Site-to-site VPN.defn: Tunnel connecting whole networks, often IPsec tunnel mode

SSL VPN.defn: Browser-based or TLS remote access, no client install

Split tunnel.defn: Only some traffic traverses the tunnel

ZTNA.defn: Per-request verification — no implicit network trust

SASE.defn: ZTNA + SD-WAN delivered as a service

PFS.defn: Perfect forward secrecy — ephemeral keys, past traffic stays secret

HSTS.defn: Tells browsers to refuse plaintext connections

DNS filtering.defn: Blocks access to known malicious or policy-breaking domains

EDR.defn: Endpoint detection and response, behaviour-based monitoring

Allowlisting.defn: Only pre-approved software runs, blocks unknown malware

Blocklisting.defn: Known bad software is denied, misses unknowns

Code signing.defn: Verifies software origin and integrity before execution

Secure baseline.defn: A documented secure configuration from a known state

CIS benchmark.defn: Consensus security configuration guidance from CIS

MDM.defn: Mobile device management, enrol, configure, enforce, wipe

BYOD.defn: Bring your own device, corporate data on personal devices

Application vetting.defn: Assessing and approving apps before corporate install

Secure boot.defn: Verified boot chain blocks tampered firmware

Shift left.defn: Security from the first design, not the last test

Threat modelling.defn: Finding the attack surface before code exists

DevSecOps.defn: Security in the CI/CD pipeline, not a release gate

SQL injection.defn: User input treated as part of the query

XSS.defn: Attacker script runs in another user's browser

CSRF.defn: Forged request rides a victim's session

Sandboxing.defn: Isolating code to contain any compromise

Directory traversal.defn: Dot dot slash escapes the web root

IaaS / PaaS / SaaS.defn: Infrastructure / platform / software as a service

Community cloud.defn: Shared by organisations with common needs

Shared responsibility.defn: Vendor secures the cloud; you secure what is in it

Hypervisor.defn: Type 1 bare metal or Type 2 hosted, separates the VMs

VM escape.defn: Breaking out of the guest into the hypervisor host

Credentialed scan.defn: Scan using valid credentials to see internal state

CVSS.defn: Common Vulnerability Scoring System: severity score from base, temporal and environmental metrics

CVE / NVD.defn: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures / National Vulnerability Database

Compensating control.defn: Alternative mitigation when patching is impossible

Risk acceptance.defn: Documented decision to tolerate a known risk

Responsible disclosure.defn: Vendor notified and given time before public release

Rules of engagement.defn: Written authorisation and scope for penetration testing

RTO.defn: Recovery time objective: how fast to recover

RPO.defn: Recovery point objective: acceptable data loss

MTBF.defn: Mean time between failures: a reliability measure

Failover.defn: Automatic switch to a standby system on failure

Incremental backup.defn: Changes since the last backup: slow restore chain

Differential backup.defn: Changes since the last full backup

HA cluster.defn: High availability: failover with minimal interruption

Hot / warm / cold site.defn: Immediate, partial or empty recovery facility

Overwrite / degauss / shred / cryptoshre.defn: Data destruction by replacement, magnetism, physical or cryptographic means

Chain of custody.defn: Records of asset transfer and disposal

SIEM.defn: Aggregates and correlates monitoring sources into one view

IR lifecycle.defn: Preparation, detection, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned

Incident classification.defn: Type — unauthorised access, malware, DoS, data breach

Severity.defn: Low to critical — grades the urgency of response

Containment.defn: Stopping the spread — isolate and segment

Eradication.defn: Removing the cause from the environment

After-action review.defn: Post-incident review of what worked, what failed, what changes

Root cause analysis.defn: Finding the underlying source so the incident cannot recur

Order of volatility.defn: Capture the most volatile data first — RAM before disk

Imaging.defn: Bit-for-bit copy — analyse the copy, preserve the original

Write blocker.defn: Prevents any change to the original data during examination

Memory forensics.defn: Analysing RAM — running processes, open connections, remnants

File carving.defn: Recovering files from raw disk without the filesystem

Metadata analysis.defn: File creation dates, authorship, modification history

C2 beacon.defn: Regular small connections to a command-and-control host

Impossible travel.defn: Logins from locations too far apart in time

Policy.defn: High-level intent — what must be achieved

Regulatory compliance.defn: Required by law — GDPR, PCI DSS

Qualitative risk.defn: Ratings and judgement — high, medium, low

Data sovereignty.defn: Data is subject to the law where it resides
